prompt: Read the Finnish sentence: 'Kaikki eivät läpäisseet tenttiä.' Does this mean: (a) Nobody passed the exam, (b) Not everybody passed but some did, or (c) Everybody passed? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.

Read the Finnish sentence: 'Kukaan ei läpäissyt tenttiä.' Does this mean: (a) Nobody passed the exam, (b) Not everybody passed but some did, or (c) Everybody passed? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Minimal pair for fi-neg-001a: 'kukaan' (negative-polarity existential, singular connegative agreement) negates an existential claim, unlike 'kaikki' (universal, plural agreement) in the paired item, so the correct reading flips from 'not everybody, but some did' to 'nobody passed'. Same construction family (connegative + ei), different quantifier host -- isolates whether the model tracks which quantifier is under negation rather than pattern-matching connegative structures to one default reading. Requires native-speaker naturalness review.

prompt: Read the Finnish sentence: 'Kaikki eivät tulleet kokoukseen ajoissa.' Does this mean: (a) Nobody arrived at the meeting on time, (b) Not everybody arrived on time, but some did, or (c) Everybody arrived on time? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Second lexical instantiation of RULE_FI_NEG_CONNEGATIVE, using 'arriving at a meeting on time' instead of 'passing an exam' so the category isn't validated on a single predicate. Requires native-speaker naturalness review (kept in the animate/person domain since 'kukaan' in the paired item requires a person referent).

prompt: Read the Finnish sentence: 'Kukaan ei tullut kokoukseen ajoissa.' Does this mean: (a) Nobody arrived at the meeting on time, (b) Not everybody arrived on time, but some did, or (c) Everybody arrived on time? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
